thread:
omar: quick flag: packaging PR that tightened exports map caused a couple onboarding flows to break in edge/bun/deno CI jobs. Node local tests passed so it slipped by.
helena: saw the failing CI runs. what's the common failure?
omar: two categories: (1) edge runtimes throw ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on root import; (2) deno complains "package does not provide an entry point" for npm: specifiers. bun fails similarly when resolving package root.
sam: rough cause is we only exported explicit subpaths (./client, ./server) and removed the root (.) entry. lots of starter apps still import the package root.
helena: can you paste what we shipped?
omar: shipped snippet (simplified):
```json
"exports": {
  "./client": "./dist/esm/client.js",
  "./server": "./dist/cjs/server.js"
}
```
sam: that blocks users doing `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` and tools that read ./package.json.
helena: immediate patch idea?
omar: add a permissive root export with import/require/types, expose ./package.json, and a wildcard for subpaths. e.g.:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js","types":"./dist/types/index.d.ts"},
  "./*":"./dist/*",
  "./package.json":"./package.json"
}
```
sam: +1. Also add `main` and `module` back to package.json for legacy bundlers and CDNs that don't use exports.
helena: longer term, we should prevent this from recurring. suggestions?
omar: two things: (A) add an exports-checker in the SDK packaging pipeline that validates the map contains `.` and `./package.json` and that types point to an existing .d.ts file; (B) add a small CI matrix in sample-apps that runs bun build, deno bundle (npm:), and an edge smoke test (Miniflare or wrangler) to catch edge resolver differences.
sam: we can implement the checker as a tiny node script used in prepublish: it reads package.json.exports and asserts presence of keys and that targets exist on disk. fail the job with a helpful message.
helena: and add a lint rule in devex repo to look for packaging PRs that modify exports without a changelog entry.
omar: operational flow I propose: patch PR -> canary publish to staging registry -> run sample-apps CI matrix against staging -> if green, publish patch. ci-bot, can you add that to the checklist?
ci-bot: ACTIONS: (1) omar -> open patch PR with exports + types + main/module (2) sam -> add exports-check script and prepublish hook (3) helena -> add bun/deno/edge matrix to sample-apps CI (4) ci-bot -> add canary publish step to release checklist.
sam: one small runtime gotcha: some edge bundlers ignore require targets and always prefer import, so ensure our ESM build is clean (no top-level CJS). And for Deno, consider shipping a minimal `dist/deno/mod.ts` that re-exports from ESM for nicer deno:npm interop.
helena: will add a short changelog note about compatibility. mention that consumers importing root are fine after patch; if they import internal paths they should prefer the public subpath entries.
omar: I'll open the PR now and include a short repro that fails in Miniflare so reviewers can validate the fix quickly. tagging @devex and @eng-runtime for visibility.
sam: thanks — after patch lands I'll run a quick audit across our repos to catch any other packages that tightened exports the same way.
